# Files permitted to spawn a shell interpreter through os/exec.
#
# CLAUDE.md architectural rules: use argument vectors rather than interpolated
# shell commands for Git, tmux, and Docker Compose. The rule exists because a
# command handed to a shell is a command the shell may re-split, and a value
# that reached it from configuration or from an agent would then be executable
# text rather than data.
#
# Directives, one per line:
#
#   allow: <prefix>   exempts repository-relative paths starting with <prefix>
#
# Exemptions belong here rather than in a //nolint comment, so that every
# deliberate use stays visible in one reviewable place (ADR-025). Each one must
# say why the shell is the subject of the code rather than a convenience.

# The generated Claude hooks and the report helper are POSIX shell scripts,
# because Claude runs a hook by handing its command string to a shell. Their
# tests run them the way Claude does, which means running a shell.
#
# Nothing interpolated reaches these invocations: the test executes a generated
# script by path and feeds it a payload on standard input. What the scripts
# themselves contain is checked by the same tests, which require them to print
# nothing and always exit 0 (see hookScript in internal/agent/claude/hooks.go).
allow: internal/agent/claude/claude_test.go
